chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ṣalt, from Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A questioner asked him about the time of Maghrib. He said: Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, says in His Book concerning Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:
“So when the night darkened over him, he saw a star.”

So this is the beginning of the time, and its end is the disappearance of the twilight. The beginning of the time of ʿIshāʾ is the vanishing of the redness, and the end of its time is until the darkening of the night, that is, midnight.

key_terms.جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ: the onset and covering of night over a person
key_terms.ذَهَابُ الْحُمْرَةِ: the vanishing of the redness in the sky that marks the start of ʿIshāʾ
key_terms.غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ: the deep darkening of the night
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةُ الشَّفَقِ: the disappearance of twilight marking the end of Maghrib time
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight, the endpoint mentioned here for ʿIshāʾ time
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the prescribed time for the Maghrib salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the beginning and ending times of Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal times of Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ by invoking a Quranic expression about the onset of night. It identifies the beginning of Maghrib with the arrival of night, its end with the disappearance of twilight, and the time of ʿIshāʾ from the vanishing of redness until midnight.
